title: [Feature][Compile] Fuse SP matmul with reduce-scatter
body:
This PR restores the matmul + reduce-scatter (MMRS) fusion removed during the FlashComm refactor, using standard FX `PatternMatcherPass` passes.

## Native MMRS operator call

The fusion replacements call `DeviceOperator.npu_mm_reduce_scatter_base` directly. The native TorchNPU operator already supports FakeTensor/FX shape propagation, so this PR does not register an additional `torch.ops.vllm.npu_matmul_reduce_scatter` custom operator.

The direct-call update was validated with 17 targeted unit tests. A fresh TP=2 end-to-end run completed all 34 ACL Graph captures; health, model listing, chat completion, and profiler endpoints returned HTTP 200. Both TP-rank traces contained 40 `npu_mm_reduce_scatter_base` / `MatmulReduceScatterV2` calls.
## Unit tests

The six affected test files were run on CPU without requiring an NPU:

```text
188 passed, 1 skipped
```

## End-to-end and profiler validation

The fused path was validated on Ascend NPU with CANN 9.2 and `torch-npu==2.10.0.post4` using:

- Model: `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`
- TP=2 with expert parallelism and FlashComm1 enabled
- `fuse_gemm_comms=true`
- `sp_min_token_num=1`
- `HCCL_BUFFSIZE=512`
- `HCCL_BUFFSIZE_EP=512`

ACL Graph capture completed in the default `GLOBAL` mode. `/health`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/start_profile`, and `/stop_profile` returned HTTP 200, including a long-context request with approximately 8K prompt tokens.

Torch profiler and `msprof op_summary` reported 5,120 `MatmulReduceScatterV2` events on each TP rank, confirming that the fused operator executed. With `fuse_gemm_comms=false`, the SP-only control profile contained standalone `hcom_reduceScatter` events and no `MatmulReduceScatterV2` events.

The exact `/mnt/weight/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` path was not present in this CANN 9.2 validation environment, so the functional and profiler validation used `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`.

## Accuracy test

Accuracy was evaluated on GPQA Diamond using the same evaluation settings for the SP-only baseline and MMRS fusion:

| Configuration | GPQA Diamond accuracy |
|---|---:|
| SP-only baseline | 77.78 |
| MMRS fusion | 76.77 |

The MMRS result is **1.01 percentage points lower** than the SP-only baseline.

## Throughput test

The end-to-end throughput comparison used:

- Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B`
- 8 Ascend NPUs with TP=8
- Input sequence length: 65,536
- Output sequence length: 64
- Concurrency: 64

Compared with the SP-only configuration using separate GEMM and ReduceScatter operations, MMRS fusion improved end-to-end throughput by approximately **9%**.

## CANN software-stack compatibility

The supported and validated stack for this PR is CANN 9.2 with `torch-npu==2.10.0.post4`. On this stack, `MatmulReduceScatterV2` can be captured in the default `GLOBAL` mode without prior MMRS warmup, a capture-mode override, or additional communication-resource initialization.

On CANN 9.1, `MatmulReduceScatterV2` performs a synchronous `rtMemcpy` on every invocation. `GLOBAL` ACL Graph capture rejects this operation with:

```text
Synchronous memory copy failed.
This operation is supported only in RELAXED mode.
The mode set by aclmdlRICaptureBegin is GLOBAL(0).
```

Same-shape eager warmup does not resolve the failure because the synchronous copy is still performed during capture. This is therefore not a one-time communication-resource initialization issue.

| CANN version | MMRS warmup | Capture mode | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9.1 | None | `GLOBAL` | Failed |
| 9.1 | Same-shape eager warmup | `GLOBAL` | Failed |
| 9.1 | None | `RELAXED` | Capture and replay passed |
| 9.2 | None | `GLOBAL` | Capture and replay passed |

For CANN 9.1, users should upgrade to CANN 9.2 or later, disable MMRS fusion with `fuse_gemm_comms=false`, or use `RELAXED` capture for graphs containing MMRS.
